applies_why: The judge text decides a link by treating Matthew 1:16's own wording as admitting two readings rather than weighing the pressed chains against each other by footing.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: never verse by verse — one reading: a judge may not decide a link by a single verse's ambiguity; the other: a judge may note verse ambiguity if it also weighs chains by footing.
why: The judge makes the verse's two admitted readings the basis for UNDERDETERMINED, so it decides the link verse-by-verse rather than by chain-against-chain footing.
